uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. It is the number the Bank of England's 2% target is set against, and it moves gilt yields, sterling and mortgage pricing.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics reports how fast UK consumer prices rose over the year to September. The release settles whether price growth sped up or slowed in the month, and which goods and services drove the change.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the range US banks lend to each other at overnight. Dollar borrowing costs worldwide key off it, from mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The Fed raised rates at its last meeting, defying Trump's calls to lower them. This decision settles whether that hike was a single move or the first of a series, with the committee setting policy against a president who has publicly asked for the opposite.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for the countries that share the euro, meeting roughly every six weeks. Its deposit rate feeds into mortgages, business loans and the euro's exchange rate.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The Fed and the Bank of Japan raised rates within a day of each other, and this meeting settles whether the ECB moves its own borrowing costs the same way. The recent news out of Frankfurt has been about stablecoins and tokenized bonds rather than rates, so the decision itself is what shows where it stands.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, the cost of Japan's vast government debt, and the money Japanese investors hold abroad.
boj-2026-10.recent: Last month's hike was meant to curb rising prices, yet the yen fell anyway — the dollar jumped above 157 yen — and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. This meeting is the next chance to explain the path, with the Fed also raising rates and the balancing act with Bessent getting harder.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate. It anchors what British lenders charge on mortgages and business loans, and sterling moves with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The Fed and the BOJ both raised rates in September, and Brent settled near $106 a barrel. The Bank of England decides whether to move with them or hold against an oil price it cannot reach, and the answer sets the cost of borrowing for households whose loans reprice off its rate.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate, the overnight cost of dollars between banks. Its decisions reach US mortgages and loans and move the dollar worldwide.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The Fed has raised rates in defiance of Trump's calls to lower them, and the question has shifted from whether it would tighten to how far it goes. This meeting settles whether that hike was a single move or the start of a run, and whether the committee keeps setting policy against the president's stated wishes.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from the world's largest economies, hosted by a rotating presidency that sets the agenda. It makes no binding law; its weight is in who attends and what they agree to say together.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio invited Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to Miami, and the Kremlin is considering it. That puts the guest list, not the agenda, at the centre of a meeting the US hosts. It follows a Trump-Xi summit that Washington approached by capping Nvidia's compute sales to China.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council meets about every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its decisions reach borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with them.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The Fed and the Bank of Japan both raised rates in the same week, Japan's to a 31-year high. Frankfurt's own recent announcements concerned stablecoin yields and blockchain-based bonds, not borrowing costs, so this meeting is where the ECB answers whether its rate moves with theirs.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate. That rate drives UK mortgage and savings rates, and sterling and gilt yields move with each decision.
boe-2026-12.recent: The Fed and the Bank of Japan raised rates within a day of each other, and Brent near $106 a barrel is pushing up prices for every energy importer. The Bank of England's committee decides whether its own rate follows its peers upward or holds against an oil shock it cannot reach.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, the cost of Japan's vast government debt, and the flow of Japanese savings invested abroad.
boj-2026-12.recent: The last hike was meant to curb rising prices, yet the dollar jumped above 157 yen afterward and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. The board meets with a currency that weakened on a tightening move and a balancing act with Bessent still to manage, and decides whether to tighten again.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.standing: The monthly count of US payrolls, unemployment and wages, published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the main read on the labour market the Federal Reserve steers by, and bonds and the dollar move on it.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports how many jobs US employers added last month and where the unemployment rate stands. The release settles the latest reading of the labour market for everyone who prices hiring, wages and borrowing off it.
